memo.verdict: Park. Bearish on the return at this price; conviction medium. The record's thesis: Endesa is a regulated-growth re-rating that has already happened, in a yield stock; at EUR 41.34 the shares pay 16.6x consensus earnings 24 months forward, above the stock's own ten-year 'mania' band, for a business whose earnings per share grow about 4 percent a year after 2026 and whose dividend yields about 4 percent; the modal return is 1.8 percent a year over eighteen months and 4.7 percent a year over three years against a 20 percent bar. The park is on the return, not on the business; the framework's gate items do not trigger it (management C, business quality C, predictability B, trackability B). Conditions named: revisit at a price near EUR 33 (the ten-year median multiple on FY2028-weighted earnings, where the three-year modal return is about 10 percent a year); progress the case at a price near EUR 27 to EUR 32 (where the modal path clears the bar on at least one horizon); or earlier if FY2027 guidance in February 2027 is set above EUR 2.6bn, if customer additions turn positive for two quarters with the margin held, or if a ten-year Almaraz extension is granted. The record's one-line bet: a 4 percent yield and 4 percent growth at a multiple above the stock's own 'mania' band cannot return 20 percent a year, so the modal path from EUR 41.34 is a low single-digit return with a political tail. The drop-through sensitivity loses money over eighteen months even at the 'defendable' multiple, which the record calls the case for not holding the shares rather than merely not buying them.
case: The change is real, external and dated, and mostly tailwind. Spain lifted the distribution investment cap to EUR 10.2bn for 2027-2030, the CNMC raised the network return to 6.58 percent for 2026-2031 (fixed in nominal terms, below the 7.5 percent asked), Almaraz was extended to 2030 and the 7 percent generation tax suspended (EUR 104m in H1 2026). Three external forces are headwinds: retail competition and churn above 25 percent ('Competition' D: Octopus over 500,000 customers adding 170,000 to 250,000 a year, Repsol 3 million clients, independents targeting about 1.0 million, Endesa's liberalised base down from 6.9 million in 2023 to 6.2 to 6.3 million), solar cannibalisation (Iberian spot prices -48 percent to EUR 44.20/MWh in Q1 2026, solar capture EUR 25.86/MWh, 1,223 negative-price hours; H1 2026 pool EUR 49.8/MWh, -19.4 percent; 7.9 GW of batteries eroding hydro's 15 to 20 percent premium over five to eight years), and a political history of intervention in 2021, 2022 and 2023 with an election in 2027. Demand grows slowly (+1.7 percent mainland in H1 2026, +1.2 percent adjusted; August 2026 +5 percent) and cannot reach revenue until the grid is built: 94 percent of nodes saturated, 18 percent of connection requests approved. Grid equipment is a headwind to the thesis itself: transformer lead times five to six years, 63 percent of planned Spanish substations late by an average seven years, execution timelines six to seven years, double the theoretical. Balancing costs rose 34 to 36 percent to about EUR 3.2 to 3.4bn in the first eight months of 2026, EUR 22 to 23/MWh that cannot be passed through fixed-price contracts (the April 2025 blackout cost EUR 230m unrecovered).

The change inside the company is a parent's rotation and a plan refresh. A grids specialist from Enel became chief executive on 28 April 2026, confirmed the strategy unchanged, holds zero shares; five senior departures rebuilt the executive committee from Enel's pool. The February 2026 plan is articulated and resourced ('Strategy change' B): networks 47 percent of capex, renewables cut 20 percent, RAB to EUR 13.0bn, 400 MW storage, a pivot the Royal Decree later validated. Guidance was raised ('Guidance raised' B) after a FY2025 beat of EUR 351m against the original EUR 1.9 to 2.0bn target and a FY2024 EBITDA beat of 1.8 percent; the raise is to a floor fed by about EUR 200m of one-offs. Balance-sheet utilisation rises ('Balance sheet' B): 1.6x toward about 2.3x, the lowest in the peer group (Iberdrola 3.1x, EDP 3.5x, Naturgy 2.2x), at the cost of interest and EUR 3.52bn of parent dependence. Pricing is real ('Price rises' B): EUR 56/MWh, a record, earned on shrinking volume; the 2028 plan needs a 60 percent gross margin expansion for fixed-price customers that Morgan Stanley calls aggressive. Costs fall ('Standards improvement' B: fixed costs -8 percent, over 500 initiatives, cost to serve EUR 10.20). The one force turned negative is 'Shareholder returns' D: the buyback ends by mid-2027 with no extension. The one-off dependence of the base is the material internal catch-all: EUR 280m gross, about 22 percent of H1 2026 attributable income, top 5 percent of European utilities, the 'false friend' the risks research names.

'Financial Outputs' turned up once and flatten. The framework's conditional rule asks for plausible logic for continuation; the logic runs the other way: consensus FY2027 EPS -0.2 percent, FY2028 +3.7 percent; our path EUR 2.45, 2.45, 2.55. 'Goldilocks growth' F: FY2026 about +8 percent on the ordinary base (EUR 2.26 to EUR 2.45) and +15 percent on the reported base (EUR 2.10 to EUR 2.45); FY2027 flat (the buyback's about 2 percent and networks growth offsetting the loss of about EUR 200m of one-offs and an easing margin); FY2028 +4 percent; FY2026 to FY2031 about 3 percent a year; the sell-side's long run brackets ours (Jefferies 1 percent a year 2025-2030, Morgan Stanley 1 to 3 percent to 2030, Bernstein 7.4 percent 2025-2028). H2 2026 is likely to show a 15 to 20 percent decline against H2 2025 on our build. 'Sell-side upgrades' B: our EUR 2.45 sits above the guidance floor (about EUR 2.33 per share on 1,029m shares) and about 1 percent above consensus EUR 2.42; 'Upgrade record' A (the "honest tracker to conservative sandbagger"; FY2025 +17.5 percent against the initial target); 'Revision skew' B (FY2027 +4.8 percent over three months, +21.2 percent over twelve; no cut recorded); 'Guidance conservatism' B (Morgan Stanley: underlying performance "sufficient to achieve the high end of guidance"); 'Guidance vs consensus' C (guidance is a floor consensus already stands above). 'Key metrics' C: 'Revenue growth' D (+0.5 percent FY2025, +1.1 percent H1 2026, after -23.0 and -16.5 percent in FY2023 and FY2024); 'Margin' C (EBIT margin 15.7 percent FY2025, 19.0 percent H1 2026; EBITDA margin 28.1 percent FY2026 flat after); 'Cash conversion' B (FFO 70 percent of EBITDA, guided to 78 percent; capex to EUR 4,091m in FY2027 eats the FCF improvement by design); 'Net debt' D (rising by design). 'Staircase' C: near steps B (Q3 2026 results 2026-10-28 with churn metrics first; the FY2026 print; the ministerial allocation; the sixth EUR 500m buyback tranche; the generation tax phase-down; possible Almaraz confirmation); mid and far steps C (FY2027 guidance February 2027; buyback completion; TOTEX parameters; the 2027 election as likely a risk as a step; RAB EUR 13bn in 2028; a possible ten-year Almaraz extension worth EUR 5.1bn of cumulative EBITDA over 2029-2045; a new plan likely February 2029).
counter_case: At Building Block 1: Endesa is being re-rated from a yield stock to a regulated-growth stock, and the market is right to do it. Regulated activities are nearly half of EBITDA and rising. The Royal Decree lifts the cap to EUR 10.2bn; Bernstein expects Endesa's distribution capex to reach EUR 8.8bn over 2026-2030 and the RAB EUR 15.2bn by 2030, a 5.7 percent compound rate. The CNMC's 6.58 percent is a 100 basis point rise. A ten-year Almaraz extension is worth EUR 5.1bn of cumulative EBITDA over 2029-2045 and about EUR 1.9bn of equity value, about EUR 1.85 a share, and a pro-nuclear coalition in 2027 could deliver it. Supply margins are protected by 98 percent hedging of 2027 power. The sell-side's Hold and Underweight ratings are the ones it held through a 55.8 percent rally while its estimates rose 20 to 33 percent; it has been wrong on the price for a year. Iberdrola, the same mix shift two steps ahead, trades at 18.1x and compounds EPS at 7 percent. Valued like Iberdrola, with Bernstein's 7.4 percent adjusted EPS growth to 2028, at 18x on EUR 2.70 of FY2028-weighted earnings the shares are worth about EUR 48.6 plus EUR 5.30 of dividends at three years, EUR 53.9, +30 percent, 9.2 percent a year. The record concedes the mix shift (anchor 14.9x not 13.3x), concedes the sell-side's targets lagged the price for a year and may again, and concedes the post-2030 nuclear option is real and not in its numbers. It holds its view because the strongest form of the case against, at its own multiple and growth, returns 9.2 percent a year, an F; bull and bear disagree whether the shares are worth about EUR 48 or about EUR 38 in three years and neither gets near EUR 71.4; the Iberdrola comparison cuts the other way on the facts (diversified across jurisdictions, 22 percent churn against a sector above 30 percent, no large one-offs, 7 percent growth, against one regulator, one parent, 25 percent-plus churn, 22 percent one-offs, 3 to 4 percent growth); the price already pays for the regulated-growth reading (the stock at its 93rd percentile, its parent at its 50th); the sell-side's refusal to follow the price is informative (houses that raised numbers 14 to 16 percent kept Hold on "largely priced-in"); and the regulated business cannot bound the downside (enterprise value EUR 54.5bn is 4.7 times the RAB of EUR 11.5bn), which is bounded instead by the yield and the ten-year median multiple at about EUR 33. Where it would win: FY2027 consensus EPS above EUR 2.60 with the multiple above 17x through the February 2027 results; the record puts the premium holding three years at about 35 percent, possible.

At Building Block 2: the Foundations are a B because the part that matters is a regulated monopoly and retail is a sideshow: regulated activities nearly 50 percent of EBITDA and rising, an exclusive concession, a RAB compounding at 5.7 percent at a return just raised 100 basis points, 1.6x leverage against peers at 2.2x to 3.5x, ROIC 11 percent against 7 and 6; the sell-side values supply at a low multiple (5.0x EBITDA at Jefferies), so losing price-sensitive customers to independents who cannot sustain discounting is value-accretive pruning, as the margin per customer shows; management beat guidance three years, hedged 98 percent of 2027 power ahead of the sell-side, cut renewables before the solar collapse. The record concedes the regulated half is a B on its own, the pruning rational, the calls good. It holds because the thesis needs both halves: the 2028 targets require a 60 percent gross margin expansion for fixed-price customers and a base recovering from 6.3 million to 6.7 million at once, and a price-defended margin loses customers; the regulated foundation's single point of failure is the politics that granted it, with three interventions in five years; a B business compounds its advantages and this one lost 10 percent of its liberalised customers in two years with its one compounder at 5.7 percent; the good calls are those of a disciplined subsidiary executing its parent's plan. It would win on two consecutive quarters of customer additions with the margin above EUR 52/MWh; the Q3 2026 release on 2026-10-28 is the first test.
triggers: Price: revisit near EUR 33 (ten-year median on FY2028-weighted earnings; three-year modal return about 10 percent a year); progress near EUR 27 to EUR 32 (the modal path clears the bar on at least one horizon; EUR 32.3 on the eighteen-month leg, EUR 27.4 on the three-year leg). The multiple: alarm above 17.35x, the five-year high; the bearish view is invalidated by a sustained multiple above 17x with FY2027 consensus EPS rising above EUR 2.60 through the February 2027 results; below 13.3x is the shock branch and a buying level. The supply margin: alarm below EUR 52/MWh; invalidate below EUR 50/MWh (Morgan Stanley's threshold); two quarters of customer additions with the margin above EUR 52/MWh would show the franchise compounding, two quarters of losses above 100,000 with the margin below would confirm the doubt. Customer attrition: alarm quarterly losses above 100,000; invalidate above 200,000 in a quarter (the risks research's trigger); the Q3 2026 release on 2026-10-28 is the first test, churn metrics first. The lifted cap: alarm if the ministerial allocation gives Endesa below EUR 4bn or 2027 distribution capex falls below EUR 1.2bn; invalidate if the cap is reinstated; the allocation at about 80 percent odds and deployment at about 65 percent. Political and regulatory: alarm on any ministerial or CNMC draft that cuts the 6.58 percent, the EUR 10.2bn cap or the Almaraz licence; invalidate on a windfall tax or return cut enacted; intervention possible at 25 to 30 percent through the 2027 election; the TOTEX calibration pending. FY2027 guidance in February 2027: above EUR 2.6bn would be an upgrade the sell-side has not modelled and would move the setup fit to C and bring the revisit forward. A ten-year Almaraz extension (worth EUR 5.1bn of cumulative EBITDA over 2029-2045, about EUR 1.85 a share on Bernstein's figures) would bring the revisit forward. Consensus revisions: alarm on any cut of 2 percent or more; invalidate on cuts of 5 percent across years; our modal case a further 1 to 2 percent rise. Demand: alarm below +0.5 percent for two quarters. Day-ahead pool price: the risks research's trigger is a sustained price below EUR 60. One-offs: alarm above 10 percent of annual net income. The parent: alarm on a payout above 100 percent or a dividend policy change at Enel's request. The optical H2 2026 result: a 15 to 20 percent decline against H2 2025 in February 2027 would be arithmetic, not news, but may be read as a miss. Unanswered from the inputs: overlap with the framework's own track-record and lessons files and the Wisdom Library, both absent from the research; the final ministerial decision on Almaraz (a data gap in the latest research against a formal order in an earlier one); board independence (50 percent against 33 percent); peers' multiple trend (snapshot only); the churn metric (quarterly and company-reported). The near steps to watch: Q3 2026 results 2026-10-28; the FY2026 print against raised guidance; the final ministerial allocation of the EUR 10.2bn cap; the sixth EUR 500m buyback tranche; the generation tax phase-down from Q3 2026; the CNMC's TOTEX parameters; the buyback's completion by mid-2027; the 2027 general election.
